review_notes: I read the whole target file. I checked the definitions it relies on: `meridional`, `radialQuotient`, `rotZ_meridional`, and the simp-tagged `rotZ_apply_zero`. I also read MeridionalSlices.lean and grepped for other uses of `meridional_apply_zero`. The one clear problem is in the simp interface for `meridional` projections. I did not find a loop or an unwanted expansion. I did not run Lean, so the proposed `@[simp]` has not been compiled or checked for downstream effects. Other modules may use the `unfold meridional; simp` pattern for the other components, which I only partly checked.

findings.declaration: radialQuotient_eq_integral (use of meridional_apply_zero) and the surrounding `unfold meridional` pattern
findings.problem: `meridional x₁ x₃ 0 = x₁` is the canonical projection lemma for `meridional`, but it is a plain `theorem` in MeridionalSlices.lean, not `@[simp]`. Because it is not a simp lemma, every caller names it by hand with `simp only [..., meridional_apply_zero]`. The same hand-written call appears in AxisQuotients.lean, PotentialVorticity.lean and VorticityEquation.lean. Where the lemma is not named, the file instead unfolds the definition: `unfold meridional` followed by a fresh `simp [Real.cos_neg, ...]` or `fin_cases` at lines 31, 46–47, 135 and 168. The other two projections have no public lemma. `meridional_apply_one` and `meridional_apply_two` are `private` in VorticityEquation.lean, so this file cannot use them. That is why `h_simp` needs `ext i; fin_cases i`. Without simp lemmas for all three components, `simp` can only see through `meridional` by unfolding it to `![x₁, 0, x₃]`.
findings.proposed_change: In MeridionalSlices.lean, tag `meridional_apply_zero` with `@[simp]`. Add public `@[simp]` lemmas `meridional_apply_one : meridional a b 1 = 0` and `meridional_apply_two : meridional a b 2 = b`, and remove the private duplicates in VorticityEquation.lean. In this file, `simp only [radialQuotient, meridional_apply_zero]` can then become `simp [radialQuotient]`. The `unfold meridional; simp [...]` blocks at lines 31 and 46–47 can drop the unfold or the `fin_cases`. Every lemma is a direct projection with no hypotheses, and the right-hand side is strictly smaller, so there is no loop risk.
findings.benefit: `simp` normalises `meridional a b i` to a coordinate without callers naming the lemma or unfolding the definition. The ten or so `simp only [meridional_apply_zero]` call sites become plain `simp`. The `meridional` definition stays opaque to proofs. The simp set for the other two coordinates is also consistent, rather than split between a public non-simp lemma and private duplicates.

evidence.excerpt: theorem meridional_apply_zero (x₁ x₃ : ℝ) : meridional x₁ x₃ 0 = x₁ := by
private theorem meridional_apply_one (a b : ℝ) : (meridional a b : Vec3) 1 = 0 := by

evidence.declaration: same simp only call at another site

evidence.excerpt: @[expose] def meridional (x₁ x₃ : ℝ) : Vec3 := ![x₁, 0, x₃]
